input.prompt: Freeflow's settings can only be changed from Pi's settings screen. I want them changeable the same way on every host: one table of settings, a settings script the agent can run in any scope, and /freeflow settings on Claude Code. Can you build that?

required: list with nothing set shows every setting all hosts act on at its default, and names the Pi-only ones
every settable key can be set, read back and unset in each of its scopes
inherit unsets a key in that scope
a repository write drops a value equal to its default; a personal write keeps it and overrides the repository
a personal write adds .freeflow/local.json to Git's exclude first
a Session value wins over the files, lives in the Freeflow home and is gone in another session
a change prints the Runtime State lines it changed, and the prompt note for a prompt
refusals name what is wrong and write nothing
the Session scope is refused without a session ID
an invalid file stops every write and is named by list and get
a personal file Git tracks is refused
a file with v: 1 is read, and a write keeps it
outside a Git repository a personal write still works
a folder inside the repository reads and writes the repository's settings
host adapters share rendered mandatory context but emit host-native envelopes
host adapters stay inert for disabled and unsupported lifecycle inputs and report an invalid config
a config Pi accepts activates Freeflow on every hook host
the hooks and Pi agree on every config's validity
a hook host's Runtime State names the user's review choice, and only a choice
a hook host's Runtime State names the skills the user turned off, and drops an off prompt
a hook host reads the session's own settings over the files, for that session only
the shared config validator imports nothing but Node and its own files
the user selects which runtime prompts a hook host delivers
an invalid prompt selection is reported
each Claude Code hook stays under Claude Code's context cap and together they deliver every prompt once
Codex's hook limit holds the whole context
every runtime prompt fits one Claude Code hook with room to spare
the npm package Codex installs has no Agent Plugins manifest and delivers Freeflow's context
the root hooks file delivers Freeflow's context under Gemini and nothing under Claude Code
